SILENCE: Mexico Launches Renewable Energy + 935MW Storage Call via CFE
May 22, 2026

📰 While US outlets ran 15+ stories this week on cartels, ICE enforcement, and World Cup security fears, Mexico's SENER published a call for renewable energy and storage projects through CFE — 935MW of battery storage needed, projects from 0.7MW up, expression-of-interest window May 25–Aug 25.

Separately, MIP Real Assets announced $12B in infrastructure investment including $8B for renewables. Zero US mainstream coverage of either.

CNBC: Democrats Make Demands of U.S. Trade Representative Ahead of USMCA Review
May 20, 2026 | 🟡

📰 15 Senate Democrats wrote to USTR Greer insisting the USMCA failed to stop offshoring, citing Mexican manufacturing wages of "$3 to $5 per hour." The letter blames Mexico — not the US companies that chose those wages under a trade agreement Washington designed.

NAFTA created the wage gap incentive. USMCA preserved it. The July 1 review deadline approaches with both parties framing Mexico as the problem rather than the structure they built.

• "Mexican manufacturing worker pay lower than in China"
• "U.S. companies continue to offshore at alarming rates"

FOX/OUTKICK: Iranian National Team to Train in Mexico During World Cup After Base Camp Switch
May 23, 2026 | 🟢

📰 Iran moved its World Cup base camp from Tucson to Tijuana over "security concerns" and visa issues. Fox runs it straight as a sports item — but the subtext is right there: a sanctioned nation found Mexico more practical and hospitable than Trump's America.

The federation said Tijuana "resolves potential visa issues since the team will enter the U.S. through Mexico" and has all needed facilities. Iran plays Group G at SoFi Stadium in LA.

• "Uncertainty surrounding the war in the Middle East and security concerns"

NEWSWEEK: ICE Reveals World Cup Operations Amid Struggling Ticket Sales
May 20, 2026 | 🟡

📰 Newsweek runs the ICE plan and the ticket slump in the same headline — but won't say the obvious: announce armed immigration agents "every day" at matches, and mixed-status families stop buying tickets.

Thousands of group-stage seats remain unsold. Resale prices have dropped below $100 with three weeks to opening day. DHS says agents will target counterfeits and trafficking — while refusing to rule out immigration arrests.

• "We're not there to go round up mass individuals, but we are always looking for the worst of the worst"
• "ICE and HSI will be out there every day"

May 20 – May 23

1. NEWSWEEK — "ICE World Cup Operations Amid Ticket Slump" (🟡) — links enforcement plans to declining demand but won't name the chilling effect
2. FOX/OUTKICK — "Iran Moves Base Camp to Tijuana" (🟢) — Iran chose Mexico over Arizona for safety; reported straight
3. CNBC — "Democrats USMCA Demands" (🟡) — frames Mexico as low-wage competitor, ignores US-designed trade architecture
4. SILENCE — CFE Renewable Energy + 935MW Storage Call (🔴) — zero US coverage while 15+ cartel stories ran

🚨📉 US CONSUMER CONFIDENCE HITS ALL-TIME LOW — LOWEST SINCE 1952

University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index crashed to 44.8 in May — the lowest reading since the survey began 74 years ago. Down 21% since February alone.

57% of Americans spontaneously cited high prices destroying their finances, up from 50% last month. Year-ahead inflation expectations climbed to 4.8%. The Iran war's Hormuz disruption is pushing gas past $4.54/gallon.

Mexico's inflation is dropping to 4.11%. America's is climbing to 3.8%. The empire that wages war on three continents can't keep its own consumers confident.

🇲🇽📉 INFLATION DROPS TO 4.11% — MEXICO HOLDS THE LINE WHILE US PRICES SURGE

INEGI data for the first half of May: annual inflation at 4.11%, down from 4.37% at end of April. Core inflation trending down at 4.22%.

While US gas prices have surged 51% from the Iran war and American consumers report the worst confidence since 1952, Mexico's IEPS fuel subsidies keep prices stable. The same policy neoliberal economists called "unsustainable" is the reason Mexican households aren't feeling the Hormuz shock.

🇲🇽🇪🇺 MEXICO-EU DEAL SIGNED AT NATIONAL PALACE — 43,000 EUROPEAN COMPANIES ALREADY IN

Sheinbaum received von der Leyen and Costa to sign three agreements: the Modernized Global Agreement, an Interim Commercial Agreement, and a Strategic Dialogue document.

"Mexico maintains its trade agreement with the US while remaining open to other markets and foreign investment," Sheinbaum said. 43,000 European companies already export to Mexico. 11,000 operate in-country, supporting 5 million jobs.

EU Trade Commissioner Šefčovič said the EU wants Mexico among the world's top 10 economies. Bilateral trade already exceeds $94.5 billion.

🇲🇽🌽 MEXICO'S "PRECIO JUSTO" — PAYING FARMERS ABOVE MARKET TO PROTECT CORN SOVEREIGNTY

Sheinbaum signed a corn agreement covering 61,000 producers across 705,000 hectares. The problem: "Production costs us 6,000 pesos per ton while we're selling at 5,000."

The fix: companies must buy domestic corn before importing. Government compensates when international prices drop below production costs. Direct payments to farmers, no intermediaries. Registration opens tomorrow.

While the US subsidizes agribusiness giants, Mexico subsidizes the actual farmers.

🇲🇽🏛️ MEXICO FAST-TRACKS 4 REFORMS — EXTRAORDINARY SESSION STARTS MAY 26

Congress approved an extraordinary session starting Tuesday to pass four reforms in a single week. Voted 26-10 over opposition protests.

The package: postpone judicial elections to 2028 with only 2 candidates per seat (down from 10), require parties to verify candidates aren't linked to organized crime, classify foreign interference as grounds for election nullification, and strengthen electoral integrity safeguards.

Anti-narco candidacy screening + foreign interference as a nullification cause — Mexico is locking down its democracy from both sides.
